I

Ritual Stars

The appeal

First Nations girls are finishing school, with a mentor beside them every step of the way.

Indigenous girls’ education

This is who it is for.

Stars Foundation

Stars Foundation mentors Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander girls and young women in schools across Australia, from Nhulunbuy to Townsville. Nationally, only 68% of Indigenous students finish Year 12. The girls in the Stars program are changing that — in 2025, 90% of them completed Year 12.

Every Stars school has a Stars Room: a culturally safe space inside the school, with full-time mentors who work on confidence, self-esteem and life skills, and who help each girl plan what comes after Year 12. Eighty-five cents of every dollar goes straight into those programs.

The easiest way to give is to keep practising. Our Stars 5 Pack is five classes for $99, and $5 from every pack goes straight to Stars Foundation. Keep an eye out, too, for a classic raffle and a number of other fundraising opportunities popping up between now and 6 December.

Stars 5 Pack · $99$5 from every pack to StarsNow until 6 December

II

A very full Sunday

Open Day & our 11th birthday

One Sunday, two studios, every class free — and you filled them.

On Sunday 27 September we opened both studios to everyone. Eleven classes across Palm Beach and Robina — Yoga, Reformer and Mat Pilates — all free, with no pass or membership needed. 145 of you came through the doors, and eight of our teachers shared their regular Sunday classes with you.

One of the best parts was who you brought with you. Partners trying us for the first time. Friends who have always said they are not flexible enough. Neighbours who had only ever looked in through the window. Plenty of people did their very first class that day, right beside someone who already loves it — and there is no nicer way to start.

Open Day closed out our birthday month, and it was the best way we could have thought to celebrate eleven years. Thank you to the teachers who made the day happen, and to everyone who came along. If you were new that Sunday, we would love to see you again soon — the intro offers further down are the easiest way to keep going.

III

First for yourself, then for others.

Ritual School · November

Most people find their way to Ritual for themselves. A sore back, a busy mind, or simply wanting an hour in the week that is just yours. Over time the practice becomes something you rely on — a place to slow down, look after your body and come back to yourself.

And what you build on the mat does not stay there. Yoga and Pilates are mind-body practices, so the patience, steadiness and care you find in class carry into the rest of your life — into how you show up for your family, your friends and your work.

Ritual School is the next step: a chance to understand the practice more deeply, and to learn how to share it. Some graduates go on to teach. Many study simply for themselves, and find it changes how they move, rest and connect with the people around them.

A deposit holds your place and opens your classes and online content the same day, and we are happy to work with you on a payment plan that suits. Tap a training to open it.

IV

A slower start to the week

Restorative

Restorative Yoga with Rose Lamont

Monday nights · Palm Beach · 5.30pm · 90 minutes

The ninety-minute Restorative class that opened in September has settled into the timetable, and it is doing exactly what it was put there to do: taking the run out of Monday. Long, fully supported holds — bolsters, blankets and blocks doing the work so your body has nothing left to brace against.

Restorative is the slowest practice we run, and the one most people underestimate. There is no effort to it and no flexibility required. You settle into a number of thoughtfully chosen postures, stay a while, and leave feeling grounded, revived and alive.

ONENinety minutes, Monday evenings, 5.30pm at Palm Beach
TWOEvery prop provided — you bring nothing but yourself
THREESuitable for absolutely everyone, including complete beginners

If one of your Open Day guests is still deciding, this is the easiest class to bring them back to.

VI

You asked, we listened

Late cancellations
A change to the late cancellation policy

We want it to be easier to keep the promises you make to yourself. Your practice only works if you can get to it — so we have made the rules bend a little more around real life.

What it was

An eight-hour late cancellation window.

What it is now

A four-hour late cancellation period for Pass holders and Fitness Passport members, with a flat $15 late cancellation fee. Ritual Memberships go back to cancel any time.

No-shows stay as they are. And this is the first of several changes you will see roll out through October — among them, more room to breathe, with class sizes reviewed across both studios, and more events for members and the wider community.

VII

A practice to take home

Three shapes

Twenty minutes on the floor, no class required.

Spring on the Gold Coast is when everything speeds up at once — the light, the diary, the training calendar. Three supported shapes you can set up tonight with whatever is on the couch: cushions, a folded towel, a rolled blanket. Hold still, let something else take the weight, and give the body long enough to notice.

5 minutes

Supported child's pose

Knees wide, big toes together, a bolster or a stack of cushions running along your chest so your torso is held rather than hanging. Turn your head one way for half the time, the other way for the rest. Let the jaw go.

6 minutes

Supported reclined twist

Knees bent and dropped to one side onto a bolster — the prop is the point, so the knees land on something rather than pulling you over. Three minutes, then the other side.

8 minutes

Legs up the wall

Sit side-on to a wall, swing the legs up, shuffle your seat as close as is comfortable. A folded blanket under the hips if the low back grumbles, another under the head. Arms wide, palms up. Do nothing at all.

The one to do after a long day on your feet, or the night before something you are nervous about.

The rules, such as they are
  • If it aches, come out.
  • Props over effort, every time.
  • Hold each shape a little longer, rather than rushing through more of them.
And if you would rather someone else set it all up for you — that is what Monday nights are for.
